en.title: Construct a Minimum-Magnitude Sequence with Given Positive-Sum Counts
en.description: Given a sequence p of n non-negative integers, construct n pairwise distinct integers a. For any two indices i and j (i=j allowed), a[i]+a[j] must not equal 0; for each i, the number of indices j with a[i]+a[j]>0 must be exactly p[i], including j=i. Among all feasible constructions, minimize max(|a[i]|). Output any optimal construction; if there is no solution, output None. The original statement allows any optimal sequence; this site uses a semantic checker and does not require matching the examples or the reference construction.
en.input: The first line contains n, 1≤n≤100000. The second line contains n non-negative decimal integers p[i]; leading zeros are allowed. The original gave no upper bound on p[i], and this site adds no numeric upper bound; inputs with p[i]>n naturally have no solution. Very long integers may also appear; read them as text to decide.
en.output: If there is no solution, output None with exactly this capitalization; otherwise output n space-separated integers, corresponding to a[0] through a[n−1] in order, that achieve the minimum possible maximum absolute value. Do not output square brackets.
en.explanation: The original snapshot has no examples; all public examples are added by this site. For p=[0], [-1] can be output; for p=[1], [1] can be output, since its own positive-sum count is 1; p=[1,1] has no solution, because for two nonzero integers with different absolute values, the count of the one with the larger absolute value can only be 0 or 2.
hints: The zero-sum restriction means the absolute values are pairwise distinct.
Consider the sign of the sum of the item with the largest absolute value and each other item.
Peel off the items with extreme counts one by one, keeping their uniform contribution to the items not yet processed.
